member.name: T:GlitchPort.ExceptionParser
member.summary: Converts .NET exceptions into the protocol v1 exception list.

member.name: T:GlitchPort.TerminalRelay
member.summary: Starts glitchport-terminal as a child process on the first captured event and streams the line protocol to its standard input. The child is finished at most once: a broken pipe disables the relay instead of starting a second renderer.

remarks.para: The relay state lock is never held while writing to the child's stdin or while starting/killing the child. and are lock-free snapshots, so they cannot block behind a pipe write.

is idempotent and bounded: the queued relay waits at most about one second for its worker, and the child cleanup is limited to roughly two seconds (EOF grace period, kill and a bounded wait for the stdin writer to close). A renderer that stops reading stdin therefore cannot hang or process exit.
On Windows the child is assigned to a job object limited with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, so it dies with the parent process even when the parent crashes.

member.name: F:GlitchPort.TerminalRelay.ChildGracefulShutdownMilliseconds
member.summary: How long to give the child to exit after its stdin was closed (EOF) before it is killed.

member.name: F:GlitchPort.TerminalRelay.ChildKillTimeoutMilliseconds
member.summary: How long to wait for the process after it was killed.

member.name: F:GlitchPort.TerminalRelay.WriterCloseGraceMilliseconds
member.summary: How long waits for the writer close helper before it decides that a pipe write is in flight and kills the child.

member.name: F:GlitchPort.TerminalRelay.WriterCloseAfterKillMilliseconds
member.summary: How long to wait for the writer to close after the child was killed. Killing the child breaks the pipe and unblocks an in-flight write, so the close normally finishes immediately.

member.name: F:GlitchPort.TerminalRelay.ConcurrentShutdownWaitMilliseconds
member.summary: How long a concurrent caller waits for the thread that is already releasing the child. Slightly longer than the worst-case cleanup below, but still bounded.
